children: Singapore's consumer-price index likely rose 2.4% on year in September, slightly higher than August's 2.3%, according to the median estimate of economists polled by The Wall Street Journal. Core CPI, which excludes private road transport and accommodation, likely rose 2.3% in September, up from August's 2.2%, according to six of the seven polled economists. Headline inflation likely rose due to higher petrol prices, Nomura economists say in a note. Core inflation is also expected to reflect broadening price pressures from the energy price shock, they add. The data are due Friday.(amanda.lee@wsj.com)
